original_evidence.text: | Wave Terminal | github.com/wavetermdev/waveterm | **Y** — bundled `electron-updater` v6.6 | **Y automatic by default** — `autoupdate:enabled` defaults to `true`; background check runs on app start and every ~10 min while `intervalms` (default 3,600,000 ms = 1 hr) has elapsed; install-on-quit defaults to `true` (`autoupdate:installonquit: true`) | **Y** — `autoUpdater.checkForUpdates()` downloads the new build automatically on `update-available`; once `update-downloaded` fires, the app installs and relaunches via `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall()`, either on user click ("Restart") or automatically at quit if `autoInstallOnAppQuit` is set | **HTTPS**, generic electron-builder provider: `publish: { provider: "generic", url: "https://dl.waveterm.dev/releases-w2" }`; TLS certificate validation is the default (no overrides found) | **N** — the `latest*.yml` update manifest fetched from `dl.waveterm.dev` is plain YAML with no separate detached signature; its authenticity rests solely on the HTTPS/TLS session to that host | **hash-from-manifest (sha512, embedded in the manifest) + OS-code-signing** — electron-updater's standard behavior: the manifest YAML carries a sha512 of the installer/package which is checked post-download; additionally on Windows the NSIS installer is Authenticode-signed (`signtoolOptions` with `publisherName: "Command Line Inc"`, cert-hash from `SM_CODE_SIGNING_CERT_SHA1_HASH`) and electron-updater's default `verifyUpdateCodeSignature` checks the publisher name matches; on macOS the app/zip is expected to be code-signed/notarized (Squirrel.Mac requires matching Team ID) — no equivalent OS-signing gate exists for the Linux artifacts (deb/rpm/AppImage/snap/pacman), which fall back to the sha512-in-manifest check alone | HTTPS server identity of `dl.waveterm.dev` (manifest integrity/authenticity) for all platforms; additionally the "Command Line Inc" code-signing certificate (Windows Authenticode; Apple Developer ID for macOS notarization) as the OS-level trust root on Windows/macOS | emain/updater.ts:5 (`import { autoUpdater } from "electron-updater";`); emain/updater.ts:58 (`autoUpdater.autoInstallOnAppQuit = settings["autoupdate:installonquit"];`); emain/updater.ts:63 (`autoUpdater.allowDowngrade = false;`); emain/updater.ts:126-134 (`start()` — sets 600000ms poll `setInterval`, calls `checkForUpdates(false)`); emain/updater.ts:160 (`const result = await autoUpdater.checkForUpdates();`); emain/updater.ts:203-209 (`installUpdate()` → `autoUpdater.quitAndInstall();`); electron-builder.config.cjs:120-123 (`publish: { provider: "generic", url: "https://dl.waveterm.dev/releases-w2" }`); electron-builder.config.cjs:98-106 (Windows `signtoolOptions`); package.json:92 (`"electron-updater": "^6.6"`); pkg/wconfig/defaultconfig/settings.json (fetched via GitHub raw, 2026-08-20): `"autoupdate:enabled": true, "autoupdate:installonquit": true, "autoupdate:intervalms": 3600000` | Only terminal in this batch with a real self-update mechanism. The scheme is the standard, reasonably solid `electron-updater` generic-provider pattern (HTTPS transport + sha512 manifest hash + OS code-signing on Win/macOS); its weakest point is the Linux artifact channel, where the only integrity gate is the sha512 hash embedded in a manifest that itself has no independent signature — full trust chain there reduces to "TLS to dl.waveterm.dev". |
